entities.name: Grubhub
entities.description: Online food ordering and delivery platform partnering with Genuin to power offsite video sponsored posts and takeovers for its restaurant network on brand partner destinations.

entities.name: iHeart
entities.description: Brand partner destination where the Genuin SDK runs to serve short-form restaurant sponsored posts; first launch destination for the Grubhub integration.

entities.name: McDonald's
entities.description: Cited as an example of an enterprise merchant served via National / Brand Sponsorships in the Grubhub × Genuin integration.

entities.name: YouTube
entities.description: External video source supported by the BCC Admin Portal for URL-based video imports into Genuin's content store.

entities.name: Vimeo
entities.description: External video source supported by the BCC Admin Portal for URL-based video imports into Genuin's content store.

entities.name: ID5
entities.description: Third-party deterministic identity provider, email-based and strong in logged-in environments, available as an option for resolving identity in SMB campaigns.

entities.name: UID 2.0
entities.description: Open-source deterministic identity standard from the IAB Tech Lab, available as a third-party resolution option for the Grubhub × Genuin identity matching layer.

entities.name: LiveRamp ATS
entities.description: Cross-device identity graph offering both deterministic and probabilistic matching with broad publisher reach, used as a third-party resolution option.

entities.name: Lotame Panorama
entities.description: Cookie-free probabilistic identity provider relying on contextual and behavioural signals, available as a third-party resolution option.

entities.name: Epsilon CORE ID
entities.description: Deterministic identity provider that is PII-based at source but produces a privacy-compliant output ID, available as a third-party resolution option.

entities.name: Genuin SDK
entities.description: Client SDK that initializes within the brand partner's destination, requests a personalised video feed, collects non-PII signals, and renders sponsored videos when the placement enters viewport.

entities.name: Genuin Backend
entities.description: Server-side platform that receives feed requests from the SDK, prepares the identity payload, routes calls to Grubhub's recommendation endpoint, and assembles the final video feed.

entities.name: Grubhub Backend
entities.description: Grubhub's server-side recommendation and identity-resolution system that receives non-PII signals from Genuin and returns the most relevant restaurant name.

entities.name: BCC Admin Portal
entities.description: Genuin's admin portal supporting manual drag-and-drop video uploads up to 2GB and URL-based imports; also where the is_active flag per Community is managed.

entities.name: RSS / MRSS Feed
entities.description: Standard feed-based programmatic ingestion path pulled from a partner URL on a configurable schedule; the primary programmatic ingestion path for Phase 1.

entities.name: JSON Endpoint
entities.description: Partner-provided JSON endpoint that Genuin polls on a configurable schedule, returning a videos array; field name mapping is supported and the path is scoped for Phase 2.

entities.name: Genuin Content Store
entities.description: Central content repository where the three video ingestion paths converge and from which video metadata is later retrieved.

entities.name: Runtime Flow
entities.description: Seven-step server-to-server request/response cycle from SDK initialization on the partner destination through viewport-triggered video render, with Step 4 as the key Grubhub recommendation junction.

entities.name: Video Metadata Retrieval
entities.description: Nightly batch process by which Grubhub pulls Genuin's paginated video catalogue via REST API and refreshes its local mapping table using cursor-based pagination.

entities.name: Identity Matching
entities.description: Process of resolving the viewing user from non-PII signals (IP, user agent, device, OS, browser/bundle ID) via either Grubhub native match or a third-party identity graph; required for SMB sponsorships.

entities.name: Genuin Pixel
entities.description: Optional Genuin tracking pixel deployed on landing pages and purchase events to extend measurement into full-funnel landing-page visits and actual sales.

entities.name: REST API
entities.description: Paginated Genuin REST endpoint accepting page, page_size, and community_id parameters and returning a video array plus next_page_token for cursor-based pagination.

entities.name: Webhook
entities.description: Planned Phase 2 real-time webhook that allows Genuin to push video_updated events to Grubhub on publish or removal, replacing reliance on the nightly batch.

entities.name: Phase 1
entities.description: Initial launch phase: one restaurant equals one Community with exactly one Group containing one is_active video; serving uses restaurant-name lookup with no video identifier.

entities.name: Phase 2
entities.description: Follow-on phase lifting the one-video constraint, supporting multiple Groups and videos per Community, plus webhook ingestion, JSON endpoint, and a partner video selection signal.

entities.name: Community
entities.description: Top-level container in Genuin's content hierarchy corresponding directly to one restaurant; identified by a Genuin UUID and mapped to a Grubhub restaurant name.

entities.name: Group
entities.description: Mid-level container within a Community holding a thematic collection of related videos (e.g., Spring Menu, Limited Offers); in Phase 1 each Community has exactly one Group.

entities.name: Sponsored Video
entities.description: Individual short-form restaurant video clip within a Group; in Phase 1 exactly one video per Group carries the is_active flag and is served by the integration.

entities.name: Offsite Video Sponsored Post
entities.description: Core Genuin ad product that serves short-form sponsored restaurant videos within brand partner destinations such as iHeart, off the Grubhub app.

entities.name: Takeover
entities.description: Higher-prominence sponsored placement format offered alongside offsite sponsored posts in the Grubhub × Genuin partnership.

entities.name: National / Brand Sponsorships
entities.description: Sponsorship product targeted at broad US audiences using brand creative and enterprise merchants (e.g., McDonald's, March Madness offers); identity matching is not required.

entities.name: SMB / Local Sponsorships
entities.description: Sponsorship product for independent restaurants with localised delivery coverage, served to users in matching ZIP codes or neighbourhoods and requiring identity resolution.

entities.name: March Madness
entities.description: Cited example of a national brand offer/creative that would run via Grubhub's National / Brand Sponsorships on Genuin's offsite placements.

entities.name: Measurement & Attribution
entities.description: Out-of-the-box Genuin metrics (placement views, video views, 25/50/75/100% completion rates, clicks, CTR) plus optional full-funnel measurement via Genuin pixels on landing-page and purchase events.

entities.name: Broad US Audience
entities.description: National audience targeted by National / Brand Sponsorships, served without precise location matching or identity resolution.

entities.name: ZIP-Targeted Local Audience
entities.description: Hyperlocal audience resolved by ZIP code or neighbourhood for SMB campaigns; requires Grubhub identity signals to match users to nearby restaurants.

relationships.description: Grubhub partners with iHeart, the first brand partner destination where the Genuin SDK serves Grubhub's restaurant sponsored videos.
The Genuin SDK runs within the iHeart destination rather than inside the Grubhub app.
Genuin's backend prepares the identity payload and routes feed requests to Grubhub's recommendation endpoint over a server-to-server call.
The Genuin SDK sends its feed request — including non-PII user signals — to the Genuin Backend, which orchestrates the downstream Grubhub call.
Step 4 of the Runtime Flow performs identity matching and recommendation lookup inside Grubhub's backend before the restaurant name is returned.
The Runtime Flow's key Step 4 junction calls into Grubhub's recommendation engine to resolve the user's identity and the most relevant restaurant.
Path 1 ingestion: manual drag-and-drop uploads and URL imports from the BCC Admin Portal land in Genuin's content store.
Path 2 ingestion: Genuin pulls videos from a standard RSS or MRSS feed on a configurable schedule into the content store.
Path 3 ingestion: Genuin polls a partner-provided JSON endpoint and writes videos into the content store; scoped for Phase 2.
The BCC Admin Portal supports URL-based imports from YouTube as one of its accepted video sources.
The BCC Admin Portal supports URL-based imports from Vimeo as one of its accepted video sources.
A Community contains one or more Groups; in Phase 1 each Community has exactly one Group.
A Group contains one or more Sponsored Videos; in Phase 1 each Group holds exactly one active video.
Each Community is mapped one-to-one to a Grubhub restaurant name and identified internally by community_id (Grubhub restaurant UUID).
Video metadata retrieval is implemented via Genuin's paginated REST endpoint GET /goservices/third_party/grubhub/videos with cursor-based pagination.
The nightly batch retrieves the catalogue held in Genuin's content store and refreshes Grubhub's local mapping table.
Grubhub's system runs the nightly batch metadata retrieval against Genuin to keep its local restaurant-to-video mapping fresh.
The real-time video_updated webhook is scoped as a Phase 2 capability, eliminating reliance on the nightly batch.
Option A of identity matching runs natively inside Grubhub's backend, using deterministic session matches or probabilistic device/IP heuristics.
ID5 is offered as a deterministic third-party identity option when Grubhub's native match rate is insufficient.
UID 2.0 is offered as a deterministic third-party identity option for cross-device resolution.
LiveRamp ATS is offered as a deterministic/probabilistic cross-device identity option.
Lotame Panorama is offered as a cookie-free probabilistic identity option using contextual and behavioural signals.
Epsilon CORE ID is offered as a deterministic third-party identity option with privacy-compliant output.
National / Brand Sponsorships are one of the two campaign types served via the offsite video sponsored post product.
SMB / Local Sponsorships are the second campaign type served via the offsite video sponsored post product.
SMB campaigns require identity resolution so Grubhub can match users to nearby restaurants by ZIP or neighbourhood before serving.
National / Brand Sponsorships target a broad US audience and do not need precise location matching.
SMB / Local Sponsorships target users in specific ZIP codes or neighbourhoods that match a restaurant's delivery coverage.
McDonald's is cited as an enterprise merchant example for National / Brand Sponsorships.
March Madness offers are cited as an example of brand creative running under National / Brand Sponsorships.
The Genuin Pixel extends out-of-the-box measurement into full-funnel landing page visits and purchase events.
Measurement & Attribution metrics (views, completion rates, clicks, CTR) are reported by default for offsite video sponsored posts.
Takeovers are offered alongside offsite video sponsored posts as a higher-prominence placement format.
The BCC Admin Portal is where the is_active flag for the single Phase 1 video per Community is managed.
Phase 1 uses RSS/MRSS with standard fields only as the primary programmatic ingestion path.
Phase 2 introduces the JSON endpoint ingestion path with richer programmatic integration.
Phase 1 constrains the model to one restaurant per Community with exactly one Group and one is_active video.
Phase 2 lifts the one-video constraint, allowing multiple Groups and videos per Community.
